title: An infrared view of the Lupus 3 region
caption: The Lupus 3 region, imaged by ESO's VISTA survey telescope
celestial: Lupus 3 · constellation Scorpius · about 600 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Colorful clouds of gas and dust fill this image of the Lupus 3 region, where new stars are being born.

Star-forming regions like this are usually hidden behind their own dust, which blocks visible light. The picture uses infrared observations instead, and infrared light can pass through the dust far more easily, revealing new details in the star-forming areas that are normally obscured.

The data came from the VIRCAM instrument on the VISTA telescope at ESO's Paranal Observatory in Chile. The observations were made as part of the VISIONS survey, which aims to help astronomers understand how stars form inside these dust-shrouded regions. The image was taken through J, H and Ks filters in the near-infrared. The official caption offers few further details.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (37.34 x 34.45 arcminutes) and distance (600 light years), the frame spans roughly 6.5 × 6 light-years. Its light set out about 600 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This near-infrared image comes from VIRCAM on VISTA, using J, H and Ks filters. The source does not publish which color was assigned to each filter.
